findings.evidence: Row claims version_status="published" with version="40-tasks". Per c2, "published" requires the maintainer to publish a release identifier for this board that the version copies. SOURCE 1 (index page), SOURCE 3 (README) and SOURCE 2 show no release identifier or version tag for the benchmark (e.g. no vX.Y / release number); the README only gives dates ('Initial release ... 40 tasks', 2026-03-19) and the task count. An excerpt that publishes no release identifier supports "snapshot", not "published".
findings.repair: Either supply packet evidence that the maintainer publishes a release identifier this version copies, or change version_status to "snapshot" (with version of the form snapshot-<date> freezing the observed 40-task methodology).

uncertainties: Owner-computed SHA-256 bindings, transport and qualification checks are executed separately by the owner and were not verified by me.

SOURCE 1's visible excerpt contains no task list or score values; the version_guard's continuation conditions (keys, 40 ids, 0–100 scores, app.js mean ranking) are supported only by the app.js excerpt (plain mean of finite scores, ranking metric) and README's 10 domains × 4 tasks = 40 structure; the literal keys {tasks, agents, scores, frontier} appear on the page but the leaderboard.json body itself was not excerpted.
Served values 12.41–21.12 (SOURCE 5) lie within the row's stated [0,100] range and do not contradict unit 'points' or the bounds; per c1 this settles only the scale question.
README says 70+ = surpass the paper while the page says 100 = surpasses it; the row's notes already record both statements, so no contradiction in the row itself.
Scores are judged benchmark observations (LLM-judged rubric); per-served-value transcription was not required because the packet supplies no per-row benchmark-observation rows to compare.
